event: Shorter presents the melody without Davis.
relation: Initial single-horn presentation.

event: Ride-cymbal interjections against the final sustained A3.
relation: Closing four bars become an interaction site; preparation of later textures is an interpretation.

event: Davis joins Shorter; ride-bell attacks accompany the entrance.
relation: Brighter drum timbre coincides with thickened horn texture. Visual anticipation by Williams is unverified.

event: Piano chords at dotted-quarter intervals; drum punctuation in the final bar.
relation: Cross-beat grouping across the closing passage; possible coordination of punctuation.

event: Cycle boundary.
relation: Anchor for the following events.

event: Piano durations span two eighth-note-triplet units; accented repeated E-flats.
relation: A rhythmic layer against the prevailing pulse.

event: Hancock animates the accompaniment; Williams subsequently takes up its dancing quality.
relation: Meehan explicitly interprets this as uptake. Do not equate it automatically with the 1:25 event.

position: Cycle 3 closing passage; exact measure pending
event: Long–short accented, ringing ride-cymbal scrape; similar paired piano chords follow into cycle 4.
relation: Proposed drum-to-piano imitation crosses the cycle boundary.

event: Cycle boundary.
relation: Anchor; cymbal gesture from preceding cycle continues.

event: Two piano chords in the melodic rest; blues-like flat-13 voicing over the identified D7-sharp9/B-flat.
relation: Piano introduces a blues-associated color in the melodic gap; voicing needs transcription.

event: Davis gives the last note a downward growling glissando; piano follows with C–C-sharp, then F–E dyads. Drums mix swung and straight eighths.
relation: Proposed transfer from vocal trumpet inflection to piano semitone dissonance; final A7 alteration unresolved.

event: Cycle boundary.
relation: Anchor for triplet exchange and literature events.

event: Ascending quarter-note triplets in piano.
relation: Hancock introduces the rhythmic material taken up below.

event: Quarter-note triplets on toms.
relation: Williams appears to take up the piano rhythm in a different timbre.

event: Five-note spang-a-lang-like tom figure on an eighth-note-triplet grid; subsequent diminution.
relation: Rhythmic uptake is transformed in grouping, duration and drum placement.

event: Horns extend A-flat after legato delivery; Hancock lays out; Williams lowers his dynamic.
relation: Meehan links horn extension to accompaniment withdrawal and a dynamic valley.

event: Loud rimshot in the melodic gap; clearer swing returns; horns deliver B-flat strongly.
relation: Proposed drum-to-horn response. Reassurance and confidence describe an interpretation, not a verified mental state.

event: Williams plays a strong fill into a new chord; ensemble attacks with renewed intensity.
relation: Meehan reports a coordinated intensification after the valley. Keep distinct from the 2:45 rimshot.

event: Heavier, more pointed horn attacks, without shorter durations or staccato.
relation: Attack profile changes independently of note length; no specific literature corroboration located.

event: Drums take greater liberties.
relation: Specify rhythmic departures through further listening.

event: Ascending chromatic piano figuration over the identified A7-flat9-flat13 turnaround.
relation: Boundary-directed piano gesture; chord and pitches await transcription.

event: Quieter horns, longer sustained notes and fewer intervening rests.
relation: Changes in dynamics and spacing; exact span still open.

event: Ensemble diminuendo before the more active subsequent drum passages.
relation: Meehan groups cycles 9–11 as intensified drum activity.

event: New piano figuration, louder horns and changed drum interaction.
relation: Multiple parameters change near the cycle boundary.

event: Repeated intrusive snare hits interject into melodic phrases.
relation: Drums gain foreground prominence.

event: Repeated-snare activity effectively becomes a three-bar drum solo.
relation: Perceived drum foregrounding; not a claim that all other instruments stop.

event: Drum roll into the cycle; Davis leads, Shorter follows roughly 1–1.5 quarter-note beats later.
relation: Canon-like melodic displacement; strict canon and response to the roll are unverified.

event: Piano eighth-note trill figuration and glissandos; cymbal intrusions.
relation: Interventions overlap or interrupt the horn melody.

event: Ensemble diminuendo with softer piano trilling.
relation: Hancock as initiator is a response hypothesis.

event: Both horns absent; simple whole-note piano chords, prominent drums and later drum roll.
relation: Melodic withdrawal redistributes foreground activity.
source: Goldford; Meehan p. 162 n. 512; Pasceri title-track paragraph

event: Both horns return together, stately and authoritative; rhythms heard as adhering to notation.
relation: Restoration of coordinated melodic delivery; comparison with a specified score remains pending.

event: No new horn statement; drums and bass continue briefly into a fade.
relation: Released-recording ending, without an invented collective stop cue.
